title: The Compass of the Palatinate
premise: In the Rhineland winter of 1918, Kestrel Yarrow ferries letters for a suffragist press in the Palatinate, reading each one before it leaves his hands. When a census taker's probing question exposes the hidden network of deserters and displaced families sheltering in the old workshop, Kestrel must choose between the woman who taught him to read the world and the found family the workshop protects. As the armistice teeters on rumor and the census becomes a pretext for conscription raids, he races to finish printing a final pamphlet of names — a record of everyone the war tried to erase. The workshop burns on the last night; the pamphlet survives, carried out in a satchel Kestrel once measured for exactly what could be carried, and the family scatters but endures, bound by the names.
about_author: Jude Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence from the Rhineland. The Compass of the Palatinate is their second novel, written in a converted coach house that once stored letters no one claimed.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Kestrel Yarrow's POV. He drives for suffragist editor Margarethe Voss, delivering mail through occupied Kaiserslautern while quietly reading every letter — his private map of who owes whom. The workshop doubles as a shelter he pretends not to see. Emotional beat: wary belonging; Kestrel keeps one foot out the door, measuring exits.

chapters.title: The Census Taker's Question
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A polite census taker, Herr Brandt, asks about residents 'not on the ration rolls' and lingers too long at the workshop door. Margarethe deflects him, but Kestrel realizes the shelter's existence is now a matter of record somewhere. Emotional beat: the safe world cracks; Kestrel's habit of reading everything becomes a liability he can't unread.

chapters.title: Names in the Margin
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Ilse, a teenage deserter's sister hiding in the loft. She discovers Kestrel reading letters and, instead of betraying him, asks him to read her brother's last one aloud. They begin a secret ritual: recording the names of the displaced in the margins of proof sheets. Emotional beat: found family forms in whispers.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Conscription raids begin in neighboring towns; Brandt returns with a list and a smile. Margarethe orders the press to print a final pamphlet — a register of the sheltered, to be smuggled out if the worst happens — but the type is short and paper scarcer than bread. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She and Kestrel forage paper from a shuttered schoolhouse, nearly caught by a patrol. Ilse confesses she's the one who told Brandt the workshop had 'many beds' — not knowing what it meant. Emotional beat: guilt and forgiveness; Kestrel must decide whether survival justifies betrayal.

chapters.title: Armistice, or Isn't
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Rumors of an armistice split the household: some want to flee while roads are open, others hold for the printing. Margarethe collapses under strain and Kestrel, the driver, must lead for the first time. Emotional beat: reluctant leadership; the compass points at people, not places.

chapters.title: Brandt's Bargain
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Brandt offers immunity for the workshop in exchange for the name list — a clean census, a quiet betrayal. Kestrel stalls him with forged entries, buying nights of printing at the cost of becoming the liar he once only read about. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in small corruptions.

chapters.title: The Last Night of Typesetting
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The household works by candlelight to finish the pamphlet as boots sound in the street. Ilse sets her brother's name last, and Margarethe, recovering, insists every name be set in full — no initials, no erasures. Emotional beat: fierce tenderness; the work becomes a vow.

chapters.title: Fire and Satchel
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The raid comes at dawn; the workshop burns as the pamphlet's final copies are pulled from the press. Kestrel carries the satchel of names through the smoke while Margarethe stays to face Brandt and the ledgers burn around her. Emotional beat: climax — everything measured against what can be carried, and what cannot.

chapters.title: The Compass of the Palatinate
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, months later. The war is over; the pamphlet circulates hand to hand, reuniting scattered shelterers. Kestrel finds Margarethe alive in a neighboring village, and Ilse waiting with a new press and a blank first page. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging is not a place that stands, but the names you refuse to let burn.
